views.name: planet_nodes_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS id,
  "version" AS version,
  "username" AS username,
  "changeset" AS changeset,
  "visible" AS visible,
  "osm_timestamp" AS osm_timestamp,
  "geometry" AS geometry,
  "all_tags" AS all_tags,
  "latitude" AS latitude,
  "longitude" AS longitude
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_NODES
views.description: Normalized projection of PLANET_NODES that exposes common node attributes with clean aliases and parses tags/geometry-ready fields. Use as a standardized node input for joins, aggregations, and time/version analytics. | Use for: node-level attribute queries (who edited node X, when, version history); spatial joins between nodes and ways/relations; aggregations by user/changeset/time on nodes

views.name: planet_ways_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS id,
  "version" AS version,
  "username" AS username,
  "changeset" AS changeset,
  "visible" AS visible,
  "osm_timestamp" AS osm_timestamp,
  "geometry" AS geometry,
  "all_tags" AS all_tags,
  "nodes" AS nodes
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_WAYS
views.description: Normalized projection of PLANET_WAYS exposing way metadata and nodes VARIANT. Use as canonical way input for joins to nodes, feature extraction, or temporal analyses. | Use for: way metadata lookups and audits (who changed a way, when); expand nodes VARIANT to join node coordinates; aggregate ways by tag or editor

views.name: planet_relations_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS id,
  "version" AS version,
  "username" AS username,
  "changeset" AS changeset,
  "visible" AS visible,
  "osm_timestamp" AS osm_timestamp,
  "geometry" AS geometry,
  "all_tags" AS all_tags,
  "members" AS members
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_RELATIONS
views.description: Normalized projection of PLANET_RELATIONS exposing members and tags with canonical aliases. Use as the base relation input for member expansion and relation-level analytics. | Use for: relation member expansion and joins to member entities; relation-level tag-based filtering and audits

views.name: planet_features_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "feature_type" AS feature_type,
  "osm_id" AS osm_id,
  "osm_way_id" AS osm_way_id,
  "osm_version" AS osm_version,
  "osm_timestamp" AS osm_timestamp,
  "all_tags" AS all_tags,
  "geometry" AS geometry
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_FEATURES
views.description: Projection of PLANET_FEATURES exposing feature identity, timestamps, and tags for feature-level analyses and joins to ways/nodes. | Use for: feature counts by type and time; join features back to ways or nodes via osm_id/osm_way_id

views.name: history_nodes_latest_per_id
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS id,
  "version" AS version,
  "username" AS username,
  "changeset" AS changeset,
  "visible" AS visible,
  "osm_timestamp" AS osm_timestamp,
  "geometry" AS geometry,
  "all_tags" AS all_tags,
  "latitude" AS latitude,
  "longitude" AS longitude,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY version DESC, osm_timestamp DESC) AS rn
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.HISTORY_NODES
views.description: Latest historical row per node id (highest version then most recent osm_timestamp) from HISTORY_NODES. Use when you need the most recent historical record per node id for audits or comparisons to planet nodes. | Use for: compare latest history row to current planet node; derive delta of node attributes versus previous versions

views.name: history_ways_latest_per_id
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS id,
  "version" AS version,
  "username" AS username,
  "changeset" AS changeset,
  "visible" AS visible,
  "osm_timestamp" AS osm_timestamp,
  "geometry" AS geometry,
  "all_tags" AS all_tags,
  "nodes" AS nodes,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "id" ORDER BY "version" DESC, "osm_timestamp" DESC) AS rn
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_WAYS
views.description: Latest historical row per way id (highest version then most recent osm_timestamp) from HISTORY_RELATIONS and PLANET_WAYS union approach is not applied here; this CTE focuses on PLANET_WAYS history access pattern. Use to get the newest history entry per way id. | Use for: get most recent way versions for spatial joins or comparison; derive world-wide latest-way counts or time-based change analyses

views.name: relation_members_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pr."id" AS relation_id,
  pr."version" AS relation_version,
  member.value:"type"::STRING AS member_type,
  member.value:"ref"::NUMBER AS member_ref,
  member.value:"role"::STRING AS member_role,
  member.index AS member_index
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_RELATIONS AS pr,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pr."members") AS member
views.description: Explode PLANET_RELATIONS.members VARIANT into one row per member exposing member type, ref id, and role. Use to join relations to their node/way/relation members. | Use for: resolve relation members to nodes/ways/relations for topology analysis; count members by type/role for relation profiling

views.name: changeset_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS changeset_id,
  "osm_timestamp_min" AS osm_timestamp_min,
  "osm_timestamp_max" AS osm_timestamp_max,
  CASE WHEN "nodes" IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE ARRAY_SIZE("nodes") END AS nodes_count,
  CASE WHEN "ways" IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE ARRAY_SIZE("ways") END AS ways_count,
  CASE WHEN "relations" IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE ARRAY_SIZE("relations") END AS relations_count
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.HISTORY_CHANGESETS
views.description: Aggregate counts of nodes/ways/relations per changeset from HISTORY_CHANGESETS table's VARIANT aggregates when present. Use for changeset-level summary dashboards or joins to changeset metadata. | Use for: identify large changesets by counts of entities; time-windowed analysis of changeset activity

views.name: planet_nodes_by_user_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "username" AS username,
  COUNT(*) AS node_count,
  MIN("osm_timestamp") AS first_activity_ts,
  MAX("osm_timestamp") AS last_activity_ts
FROM GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.GEO_OPENSTREETMAP.PLANET_NODES
GROUP BY "username"
views.description: Counts of planet nodes per username and activity time window (min/max timestamp). Use for per-user contribution summaries and leaderboards (combine with RANK CTEs downstream). | Use for: identify top contributors by node count; user activity timelines and retention analyses
